question: In the ATLS primary survey, haemorrhage control ('C' — Circulation) is assessed and managed before airway management ('A') when a patient has a life-threatening external bleed visible at presentation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The ATLS primary survey sequence — A (Airway + C-spine), B (Breathing), C (Circulation/haemorrhage), D (Disability), E (Exposure) — must be followed in order. Even with visible bleeding, airway obstruction is the more immediately lethal threat and is assessed first.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The ABCDE sequence is fixed: Airway with C-spine control is always first, even when obvious external haemorrhage is present. The rationale is that airway obstruction kills faster than most bleeding. Massive extremity haemorrhage is managed as part of C, not before A.
